St. Dimitri of Rostov

St. Dimitri of Rostov

St. Demetrius of Rostov · St. Dmitri of Rostov · St. Daniel Savvich Tuptalo

Period
1651–1709
Region

Titles / vocation
Bishop · Writer · Monastic
Commemoration

Introduction

St. Dimitri of Rostov was a bishop, preacher and compiler of saints’ lives. His education, lengthy literary work and episcopacy are central to the OCA’s account.

Read the published life [1]

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Born St. Daniel Savvich Tuptalo near Kyiv in 1651, he studied at the Kyiv-Mohyla college, learning Greek, Latin and classical subjects. He received monastic tonsure in 1668 and priestly ordination in 1675.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Opening education and ordination

Life and notable events

In 1684 the Caves Lavra entrusted him with organizing the yearly Menaion of saints’ lives. Gathering, assessing and presenting many sources occupied about twenty years. He also governed monasteries. Consecrated for Tobolsk in 1701, he was reassigned to Rostov because of frail health and his work.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Menaion and episcopal appointments

But Demetrius from his weak state of health was not capable of undertaking the journey to his distant diocese, and through the intervention of Stephen he was translated to Rostoff to take the place of the Metropolitan Joseph there deceased. From thence he was destined to illuminate by his virtues and learning the whole Church of Russia, which he edified for the space of seven years, as a zealous and uncompromising maintainer of Orthodoxy and refuter of its enemies, as an annalist, as a preacher, and above all, as a man of prayer. Thus the all-embracing heart of Demetrius united itself already with every Christian heart of his earthly country, before he began to receive prayers from those whom he had taught to pray.

Mouravieff’s1842 ecclesiastical history,Blackmore translation. Its praise and account of Demetrius’s pastoral influence are that historical author’s words.

[2] Historical reference or published author’s writing · ChapterXVI,printedp264,Demetrius at Rostoff

Death and martyrdom

The main life records his repose on October 28, 1709 and few possessions beyond manuscripts and books.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Main life conclusion

The September commemoration describes his earlier indication of a burial place at the Monastery of Saint James. Metropolitan Stephen Yavorsky instead insisted on burial beside Joasaph. The source recounts the hurried wooden support placed in the grave when Stephen had to depart; it connects that circumstance with the later uncovering.

[3] Official commemoration and received account · Burial arrangements

Writings and legacy

During repairs in 1752, the account says his body and vestments were found preserved although coffin and writing had decayed in the damp grave. It attributes subsequent healings to him and describes a Synodal investigating committee of Metropolitan Sylvester of Suzdal and Archimandrite Gabriel. The entry dates a decree of glorification to 1757 and assigns October 28 and September 21 as commemorations. Its reported miracles remain attributed to this ecclesiastical source.

[3] Official commemoration and received account · Uncovering,investigation and glorification

After ordination by Lazar Baranovich of Chernigov, his preaching took him to churches and monasteries in Ukraine, Lithuania and Belarus. The literary project required assessment of many accounts and an accessible presentation. As bishop he also addressed the division associated with the Old Believers. The OCA presents his published work as influential for later Russian theologians.

[1] Official Orthodox commemoration and received life · Preaching,literary method and ecclesial concerns

The preserved vestments named by this source are the omophorion, sakkos and mitre, together with a silk prayer rope. It also records a Russian commemoration shared with Metrophanes and Tikhon of Voronezh on July 19.

[3] Official commemoration and received account · Vestments and additional commemoration
